properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 788516

Nearest City: Chester, PA
Incident Type: STORAGE TANK
Material: OIL, FUEL: NO. 2
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: SUNOCO
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 300 gallons
FOLLOWING INFORMATION RECEIVED VIA WEB REPORT: " 1/20/01-SUNOCO DRIVER OVERFILLED/SPLIT THE OIL TANK AT 2207, LEFT THE SCENE. 1/23/01- PECO FOUND OIL IN THE BASEMENT OF 2205, BASEMENT(OF 2207).1/123/01-AROUND 200 +/- GAL OIL WAS PUMPED OUT OF 2205'S BASEMENT 1/23/01-OIL IN BASEMENT OF 2207 WAS PUMPED IN THE SEWER.1/23/01-EPA WAS NOTIFIED BUT NEVER ARRIVED, VICTIMS RECEIVED NO RELOCATIONS ASSISTANCE 1/26/01-FANNIE PENN OF 2205 WAS PERMITTED TO RETURN HOME WITHOUT ANY TESTING OF SOIL IN BASEMENTS NOR REMEDIATION TO LIVE OVER CONTAMINATED SOIL FOR 5 YEARS.3/07/01-A REMEDIATION COMPANY REPORTED STATING ONLY 40 GALLONS OF OIL WAS RELEASED AND NO FURTHER ACTION RECOMMENDED. SITE INSPECTION W/SUNOCO REVEALED OIL IN THE BASEMENT OF 2207 AFTER SAID REPORT. SUNOCO PROMISED TO RETURN AND REMEDIATE THE BASEMENT AND CORRECT DAMAGES LATTER BUT REFUSED TO DO SO.SUNOCO'S, DAVID BECKER, TOOK THIS JOB IS NOT FINISHED. FROM REPORT, AS PROOF REMEDIATION HAD BEEN FINISHED. THE COMPANY NEVER RETURNED TO DO ANY TESTING OF SOIL OR TO REMOVE THE CONTAMINATED SOIL IN THE TWO BASEMENTS. EPA STATED THEY DID NOT GET INVOLVED IN SUNOCO SPILLS, THEY ONLY HANDLE SPILLS OF SMALL COMPANIES OR PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS, SUNOCO WAS CAPABLE OF HANDLING THEIR OWN SPILLS AND ADVISED ME TO CONTACT SUNOCO, THEY COULD NOT GET INVOLVED.SEVERAL OTHER OCCASIONS EPA DID NOT OFFER ASSISTANCE NOR ADDRESS ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLATIONS. SUNOCO FINALLY RETURNED IN 2002, BUT AGAIN FAILED TO TEST THE SOIL AND WATER IN THE TWO BASEMENTS."
